newsitem.title: USA: Iridium restructures $500 mln junk deal--sources.
newsitem.headline: Iridium restructures $500 mln junk deal--sources.

text.p: Iridium LLC has tentatively retructured a $500 million junk bond offering of eight-year senior notes into two tranches, junk bond sources said.
The first tranche currently includes $300 million in 14 percent coupon eight-year senior notes, non-callable in five years, which will be priced at a discount to yield 15 percent.
The second tranche currently consists of $200 million in units that include lower-yielding debt and equity.

The debt component consists of 13 percent eight-year senior notes, non-callable in five years, which will be priced at a discount to yield 13.5 percent. The units will also include warrants to purchase a one percent equity stake in the company.
Calls to Chase Securities Inc, the lead underwriter of the offering, were not immediately returned.
Market sources noted the final structure of the offering could still change, as Chase is still negotiating with potential buyers.
Sources are saying the deal is still expected to close on Friday.
Market sources noted the latest structure of the deal is designed to appeal to two different types of buyers.
The $300 million debt-only tranche is being sold to investors looking for higher yielding junk bonds.
The $200 million unit tranche is being sold to to investors who are willing to accept a lower yield on the bonds in exchange for an equity investment in Iridium.

"The debt-only side is a blowout. Most investors are saying 'I'll take the extra yield and go out and buy the (outstanding) stock (instead of the warrants),'" said one market source familiar with the situation.
